audit.whatIsWrong: Marked EVEN at 6/10 with Sett carry threat 7/10, on a matchup Galio wins 32.26% of over 31 games — the worst number in this slice.
audit.why: A 32% win rate is not an even lane, and the page's own prose agrees: 'This is where Sett takes over', 'You never out-duel Sett one-for-one here, so stop trying'.
audit.corrected: diffRating to 8/10 and carryRating to 8/10, with the difficulty, carry and final-rating lines following. The 'diff' string still reads EVEN — it is 4 characters and every honest replacement is either the same 4 characters guessed at an enum I cannot verify, or too long; flagged rather than guessed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike says only that Sett 'out-stats your defensive AP build' — no mechanism, no numbers.
audit.why: The reason his item spike hurts a Galio specifically is Knuckle Down: 'Sett's next two attacks deal additional damage based off of the target's max health.' Galio's answer to a bruiser is HP, and HP is what that ability scales off. That inverts the usual build advice and belongs on the page.
audit.corrected: Knuckle Down (9/8/7/6/5s) named, with the max-health scaling stated so the player understands why stacking HP does not fix this lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive, entirely absent mechanics. (a) Haymaker's damage is split — true damage in the centre, physical on the sides. (b) Facebreaker only stuns when it catches enemies on BOTH sides of Sett; against one target it slows.
audit.why: Riot on Haymaker: 'Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides.' The page tells the player five separate times that Haymaker is true damage and that Shield of Durand cannot stop it — true of the centre only. Standing off-centre converts it to physical, which is the single most useful thing a Galio can do in this lane and it was nowhere on the page. Riot on Facebreaker: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a solo lane that is a slow, and it only becomes a stun once a second body is involved — which is also why the 5v5 is more dangerous than the 1v1.
audit.corrected: Eat Haymaker off-centre and it is physical. Facebreaker slows in a 1v1 and stuns only with a second target opposite you.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Haymaker with no numbers.
audit.why: Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s at 490 range, Knuckle Down 9/8/7/6/5s, The Show Stopper 120/100/80s at 400 range, against Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7s. Note Haymaker is gated by his Grit bar as much as by the cooldown, so the bar is the better tell.
audit.corrected: Numbers and the Grit-bar tell written into the cooldown block, winCon, phases[2] and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'his healing fights your trade math' without naming what heals.
audit.why: Sett has no heal — Pit Grit gives 'additional health regeneration based off of his missing health'. Naming it tells the player what they are actually buying against and when it matters (him low, out of the trade).
audit.corrected: Pit Grit named in the itemization line.

edits.before: Level 1 you have only Q Winds of War and no engage, so concede the opener and last-hit with the tip of your tornado from max range — never walk into his E grab range to throw it. The danger is his W: if you let him soak free autos and your poke, he stores it into a Haymaker that deals true damage, which your Shield of Durand barely softens — its amplified reduction is built for magic, and Sett is pure AD, so your signature panic button is weak here. Your one early answer is Level 3 — E Justice Punch knockup into a W-taunt interrupts his charge if he commits, but do not bait it unless his E grab is on cooldown.
edits.after: Level 1 you have only Winds of War and no engage, so concede the opener and last-hit with the tip of your tornado from max range — never walk into the 490 range of Facebreaker to throw it. The danger is Haymaker: he stores damage taken as Grit and spends it on a shield plus a punch that is TRUE damage in the centre and physical on the sides, so if you have to eat one, eat it off-centre. Shield of Durand barely helps — its amplified reduction is built for magic and Sett is pure AD. Your one early answer is level 3: Justice Punch knockup into a W-taunt interrupts his charge, but only with Facebreaker down.

edits.before: This is where Sett takes over. Once he hits his first bruiser item his Pit Grit double-punch and stored W out-stat your weak extended trades, and your defensive AP build just does not threaten him back. At 6 his R Show Stopper suppresses you out of your own combo — your E and W taunt get cancelled mid-suppress while his charged W lands a true-damage Haymaker, so a clean R-into-W on you is often a flat kill. Do not try to out-grit him; eat minimal poke, hold W and E for his all-in, and look to leave the lane.
edits.after: This is where Sett takes over. Once he hits his first bruiser item, Knuckle Down's next two attacks deal damage off your max health — the tankier you build, the harder they land — and Pit Grit's missing-health regen keeps him in the fight. At 6 The Show Stopper is a 400-range grab that carries you out of your own combo while a stored Haymaker lands true damage on top, so R-into-W on you is often a flat kill. Don't out-grit him: short-trade, hold W and E for his all-in, and look to leave the lane.

edits.before: You never out-duel Sett one-for-one here, so stop trying. Your value is Hero's Entrance — flag a fight in mid or bot, channel-shield your carries on the way, and drop a landing knockup-taunt on their squishies. Let your team punish an overextended Sett while you provide the engage and the frontline. By two-plus items his bruiser damage and your tankiness both start to plateau into Skill territory, so a team that respects his R-engage can play around it — but the solo lane stays his.
edits.after: You never out-duel Sett one-for-one here, so stop trying. Your value is Hero's Entrance — flag a fight in mid or bot, shield your carries on the way, and drop a landing knockup-taunt on their squishies. In a 5v5 his Facebreaker finally stuns instead of slowing, because there he has bodies on both sides of him — never stand directly opposite one of your own. Let your team punish an overextended Sett while you provide the engage and the frontline; the solo lane stays his.

notes: The page said five separate times that Haymaker is true damage and that Shield of Durand cannot touch it. Riot's text splits it — true damage in the centre, physical on the sides — so the single best piece of advice in this lane (stand off-centre) had been eliminated by the page's own simplification. Worth checking every other Sett matchup for the same flattening. I did NOT write that The Show Stopper grounds you or denies Justice Punch, even though _missing-interactions.json asserts exactly that ('Sett can deny your mobility (Justice Punch (E)) with The Show Stopper (R)'): the grounding flag on Sett's R is almost certainly a parse misfire off the phrase 'slams them into the ground' in Riot's description, which describes damage and a slow and nothing else. Same reason I softened the page's 'R Show Stopper suppresses you' to what Riot actually says — it carries you through the air and slams you down. UNVERIFIED and left alone: whether Sett's R interrupts a Shield of Durand charge, and whether Galio's taunt can be QSS'd or tenacity-shortened here. Also: full.diff still reads 'EVEN' on a 32% matchup — 4 characters, so nothing correct fits the length band; a direct edit is needed.
